requirements.text: The Enterprise Email service is being phased out ... the service has been switched to a different cloud-based platform
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_001' AND name = 'Enterprise Email' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: Enterprise Email is service SVC_001 on the seed (status operational, owned_by USER_004), the only service with 'mail' in its name
status retired kept from the benchmark check: 'phased out' and 'switched to a different platform' name no status, and retired is the seed's terminal service status (6 services carry it)

requirements.text: all Enterprise Email-related offerings are no longer supported
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE business_service = 'SVC_001' AND status = 'retired'
requirements.source: All Enterprise Email offerings are retired
assumptions: the selector picks out SVCOFF_001 (Enterprise Email - Gold) and SVCOFF_018 (Email - Silver) on the seed, both operational; no offering of another service has 'mail' in its name
status retired kept from the benchmark check; 'no longer supported' names no status and retired is the seed's terminal offering status

requirements.text: ensure that any open incidents related to this service are closed
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_004', 'INC_073') AND status = 'closed' AND resolution_code IS NOT NULL AND resolution_notes IS NOT NULL
requirements.source: No open incidents remain for Enterprise Email
assumptions: the open incidents on SVC_001 (by service or by its offerings; status neither resolved nor closed) are INC_004 (new, SVCOFF_018) and INC_073 (in_progress, no offering) on the seed
status closed from the request's 'are closed'; policy 3.3 reaches closed only through resolved (new or in_progress -> resolved -> closed), and update_incident is listed

resolution_code and resolution_notes must be set: policy 3.3 makes both mandatory for the transition to resolved, and both are null on the seed; resolution_code is tested as IS NOT NULL because the seed's values ('Solution Provided') lie outside the policy's enumeration
the set is fixed by id rather than by service = 'SVC_001', so the count stays 2 even if the agent re-links an incident
disagreement: status: A resolved, B IN ('resolved', 'closed'); chose closed because the request's words name the final state and policy 3.3 lets the agent make the resolved -> closed transition

requirements.text: any open incidents related to this service
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_018', 'INC_048', 'INC_075') AND status = 'resolved'
assumptions: boundary of 'open incidents': INC_018, INC_048 and INC_075 on SVC_001 are already resolved, so they are not open; a loose reading that closes every incident on the service would move them on to closed

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE user_id = 'USER_004' AND active = 0
requirements.source: Owner of Enterprise Email service is inactive
assumptions: the service owner is service.owned_by = USER_004 (Joanne Simpson, manager, active on the seed)
off-boarded read as deactivated (active = 0), as the benchmark check tests with active = false, which the seed stores as 0; the request names no other change to the user

No open incidents remain for Enterprise.evidence: its query tests status = 'resolved', but the request says the open incidents must be 'closed', and policy 3.3 lists resolved -> closed as a transition the agent may make, so the status becomes closed; resolution_code and resolution_notes are added because policy 3.3 makes them mandatory before resolved. disagreement: kept in one pass, repaired in the other; chose repaired because the request's words name the final state

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds a stay that none of USER_004's offerings on other services becomes retired (expected 0), the other has none; dropped because the request fixes the offerings by the service it names, no offering outside SVC_001 has 'mail' in its name, so no loose reading of 'Enterprise Email-related' sweeps another in, and the owner's 18 other offerings are tied to the task only by ownership, which the request does not use to define the set.
disagreement: value: the status of the two open incidents: one pass resolved (the benchmark's), the other resolved or closed; chose closed because the request says they must be 'closed' and policy 3.3 lets the agent reach closed through resolved.
disagreement: disposition: 'No open incidents remain for Enterprise Email': kept in one pass, repaired in the other; chose repaired, following the status decision.
disagreement: form: the stay on the three resolved incidents puts status = 'resolved' in its selector in one pass and in its cells in the other, with identical sql; kept status as a cell, since it is the column that must not change. The requirement texts differ in wording only.
Policy conflict the benchmark may have intended: its check accepts only resolved, which reads policy 3.3's closure rule (resolved incidents move to closed after 72 hours) as making resolved the agent's end state. A reviewer who takes that reading sets the incident status cell to resolved and the check's disposition to kept. USER_004 also owns 12 other services and 18 other offerings and is assigned other open incidents; the request asks for none of those to change, so owned_by on the service and offerings is not tested. The acting user USER_039 (Karen Watkins) is an active admin, so no permission rule blocks any step.
